answer: In our network, an agent economy resists Sybil attacks through game-theoretic multi-agent auditing paired with stake slashing. To validate each transaction knoll, random auditor committees run topological cut verifications across the interaction graph, treating each identity as a vertex. If colluding nodes fabricate false edges, honest auditors slash their deposited collateral. Because cut verification forces an attacker to control a bottleneck proportional to cluster size, surviving the audit gale requires superlinear attacker cost.
